title.narrative: Bogotá circular: strategy to strengthen the activity of recyclable material recoverers and innovative solutions for the solid waste management.

description.narrative: The project focuses on improving the conditions of the informal recycling population in Bogotá, who play a major role in the city's waste management by manually sorting recyclables in public spaces. The Special Administrative Unit for Public Services (UAESP), responsible for waste management, aims to formalize and support this population through training, better working conditions, and improved income. The project includes: Characterization of the Recycling Population: A survey will be developed to gather data on the demographics, working conditions, and socio-economic status of recyclers, including differentiated factors such as gender, nationality, and age. This will help tailor interventions for better support. Data Collection and Analysis: The survey will be implemented in various public spaces, targeting 11,300 recyclers initially. The collected data will be processed to create a comprehensive database, updating the UAESP's information on recyclers. Strategy Development: Based on the collected data, a strategy will be created to improve the integration of recyclers into the formal waste management system, ensuring their access to labor rights and social programs, with particular focus on women and their specific needs. Action Plan for Circular Economy: A city-wide plan will be developed to promote better recycling practices, reduce the negative impacts of recyclers' work, and promote collaboration between public and private sectors. It will include mechanisms for institutional coordination and financing. Pilot Project: A pilot will be implemented in a selected public space to improve the recycling process. The project will focus on critical waste points, safety, and minimizing negative impacts on recyclers. The involvement of homeless individuals in recycling will also be considered, as a significant portion of this population relies on recycling for income. The project aims to create a more organized, equitable, and sustainable recycling system in Bogotá, improving the lives of informal recyclers and promoting environmental sustainability.
